title: Discrete field fibres detect local quasi-finiteness of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type, tested on compatible etale scheme charts using the scheme notion [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then $f$ is locally quasi-finite if and only if, for every field $k$ and morphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$, the underlying topological space of $X_k=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}k$ is discrete [def-pc-fibre-product, def-a1-space-point-topology]. Here locally quasi-finite means that for each etale scheme chart $V\to Y$ and each etale scheme chart $U\to X\times_YV$, the scheme morphism $U\to V$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Discrete means that every subset is open; empty fibres are allowed.

proof.text: Assume $f$ is locally quasi-finite and fix $b:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$. Choose surjective representable etale scheme atlases $V\to Y$ and $U\to X\times_YV$. The sheaf fibre products are algebraic spaces, and scheme-source maps to them are representable. Composition and base change of representable surjective etale maps give a surjective etale map $U\to X$ and hence an atlas $A=U\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}k\to X_k$. Put $W=V\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}k$. Both $W$ and $A$ are schemes, $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is etale, and pullback pasting identifies $A$ with $U\times_VW$: on each test scheme both sides consist of the same compatible pair of sections.

The hypothesis on $f$ makes $U\to V$ locally quasi-finite. Its scheme base change $A\to W$ is locally quasi-finite. The etale map $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is chartwise etale: its composite with each etale scheme chart is etale by representable composition. The etale-space lemma therefore makes it locally quasi-finite. Scheme composition now makes $A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ locally quasi-finite, and thus locally of finite type.

Every point of $A$ is isolated in its fibre over the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, by the quasi-finite-point isolation lemma and the definition of local quasi-finiteness. The fibre projection is a homeomorphism onto the entire underlying space of $A$, so $|A|$ is discrete. The atlas point map $q:|A|\to|X_k|$ is open and surjective by the point-open calculus. For any subset $B\subseteq|X_k|$, its preimage is open in $|A|$ and $B=q(q^{-1}(B))$ is open. This proves discreteness, including an empty fibre.

Conversely assume all the stated field fibres are discrete. Take arbitrary etale scheme charts $V\to Y$ and $U\to X\times_YV$ and write $g:U\to V$. By the local finite-type hypothesis $g$ is locally of finite type. For every $v\in V$, let $k=\kappa(v)$, $B=U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $Z=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}k$. Scheme base change makes $B/k$ locally of finite type. Pullback pasting identifies $B$ with $U\times_{X\times_YV}Z$, so $a:B\to Z$ is representable etale by base change of the given chart. The space $|Z|$ is discrete by the hypothesis applied to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\to V\to Y$. No surjectivity of $U$ is used.

If $B/k$ were not locally quasi-finite, the field specialization lemma would give distinct $u,u^{\prime}\in B$ with $u\leadsto u^{\prime}$. The strict-drop lemma gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(u)>\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(u^{\prime})$. The point-open calculus makes $|a|$ continuous, so its images specialize in $|Z|$; discreteness forces the images to coincide. The point-fibre-product clause then supplies $r\in R=B\times_ZB$ whose projections are $u,u^{\prime}$. The space $R$ is a scheme, since both maps to $Z$ have scheme source. Its two projections $s,t:R\to B$ are etale by base change of $a$.

Composition of representable etale maps makes each of $s,t$ chartwise etale; the etale-space lemma makes each chartwise locally quasi-finite. Apply the chart transcendence-degree comparison to $R\xrightarrow{s}B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $R\xrightarrow{t}B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, using the identity scheme chart $R\to R$ and the same point $r$. Its locally finite-type target hypothesis holds by step 4. It gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(u)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(r)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(u^{\prime})$, contradicting step 5. Thus $B/k$ is locally quasi-finite for every $v$.

By the isolation lemma every point of $B$ is isolated, since $B/k$ is locally quasi-finite and locally of finite type. The scheme-fibre homeomorphism therefore makes every point $u\in U$ isolated in its $g$-fibre. Choose affine open neighbourhoods of $u$ and $g(u)$ with the former mapping into the latter, using the affine-open basis and continuity of $g$. The isolated-fibre affine-pair lemma makes the induced ring map finite type and quasi-finite at the prime of $u$. This is precisely quasi-finiteness of $g$ at $u$. Hence $g$ is locally quasi-finite; since both charts were arbitrary, the chartwise definition in the statement proves the required local quasi-finiteness of $f$.

Composition then gives A→Spec k lqf and lft, isolation plus the fibre homeomorphism make |A| discrete, and the representable surjective étale point map is open and surjective, so |X_k| is discrete.
